newsitem.title: UK: Norman to take ASDA chair, Leighton CEO.
newsitem.headline: Norman to take ASDA chair, Leighton CEO.

text.p: ASDA Group said on Tuesday Allan Leighton would become chief executive in September and current chief executive Archie Norman would take the UK food and clothing retailer'schair in December.

Patrick Gillam, 63, who took over the chairmanship of ASDA in September 1991 at the time of its financial crisis, will retire on December 19 after the company's half year results are announced, the group said in a statement.
Leighton, 43, currently deputy chief executive, will take over as chief executive on September 11 -- immediately after the company's annual general meeting.
"After five years of comprehensive change in ASDA's organisation and trading format and the development of a complete new team, the task of rebuilding ASDA is complete," Gillam said in a statement.
ASDA paid tribute to Gillam, who it said had organised the financial rescue of the company in 1991 and recruited ASDA's "extremely successful top management team".
"The share price has risen from a low of 23 pence to 116.5 pence today and ASDA has been one of the best performing shares in the FTSE 100," the group stated.
ASDA said it intended to appoint fresh non-executive directors, including a second deputy chairman.
Norman becomes full-time chairman designate until December.
